newsitem.title: USA: Fed Gov sees trend to one-stop financial services.
newsitem.headline: Fed Gov sees trend to one-stop financial services.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said the trend in the United States is moving towards one stop financial services and banks becoming involved in underwriting securities.

"People want more one-stop kind of financial services and banks are getting into securities, so I see that as sort of a natural evolution," Phillips said, answering a question about the implications of the proposed Bankers Trust New York Corp merger with Alex Brown Inc.
"We can make some changes at the margin in terms of changing the percent," she said, referring to the amount of business that banks are allowed to derive from underwriting.
"But it's going to take fundamental congressional reform if we're going to see much more movement in terms of closure of that gap," Phillips added.

The gap refers to the 1933 Glass-Steagall law that separates commercial banking from investment banking. Regulators have recently raised the limitation on how much securities underwriting a bank can do through a securities affiliate.
Phillips was answering questions after participating in a panel discussion held at Vanderbilt University here.
